title: Code supply is a portfolio of human and agent capacity

baseline.label: Human delivery baseline
baseline.interpretation: A neutral planning baseline, not a claim about lines of code or individual productivity.

supplyLayers.label: Synchronous Copilot assistance
supplyLayers.interpretation: The 55-point increment represents the published 55% faster completion result for one controlled JavaScript HTTP-server task. It is not LOC, a universal productivity multiplier, or a forecast.
supplyLayers.telemetryRecommendation: Measure task cycle time, completion rate, quality, rework, and developer experience for comparable work in your own environment.

supplyLayers.label: Copilot cloud agent
supplyLayers.interpretation: Illustrates asynchronous repository work that produces reviewable branches or pull requests; no published universal capacity multiplier is asserted.
supplyLayers.telemetryRecommendation: Track assigned sessions, completion rate, merged pull requests, median time to merge, human review time, Actions minutes, AI credits, and rework.

supplyLayers.label: Third-party coding agent
supplyLayers.interpretation: Represents an externally supplied agent integrated into repository delivery. Actual capacity and risk depend on the action, engine, permissions, tools, secrets, triggers, and review model.
supplyLayers.telemetryRecommendation: Measure run volume, accepted changes, review effort, tool denials, secret exposure paths, blocked egress, failures, cost, and incident signals by integration and version.

supplyLayers.label: Copilot SDK application
supplyLayers.interpretation: Represents product-specific agent experiences built on the Copilot CLI runtime. The number is a design placeholder, not a published SDK benchmark.
supplyLayers.telemetryRecommendation: Instrument task success, latency, token and AI-credit use, model, tool calls, permission decisions, user abandonment, quality, and business outcomes.

supplyLayers.label: GitHub Agentic Workflow
supplyLayers.interpretation: Represents repeatable scheduled or event-driven repository automation with declarative controls, safe outputs, and observable outcomes. It is not a published capacity multiplier.
supplyLayers.telemetryRecommendation: Track runs and episodes, AI Credits, turns, duration, blocked requests, safe outputs, accepted outcomes, AIC per accepted outcome, queue time, and human review effort.

contextCards.context: In a controlled experiment, 95 professional developers completed a specific JavaScript HTTP-server task; the Copilot group finished 55% faster on average.
contextCards.caveat: Task-specific measured speed, not LOC or a universal productivity rate.

contextCards.context: Historical GitHub reporting said Copilot completed up to 46% of code in files where it was enabled.
contextCards.caveat: Historical enabled-file context, not a current share of all production code.

contextCards.context: GitHub reported more than three billion accepted lines of code during Copilot's first year.
contextCards.caveat: Cumulative adoption context, not a quality, value, or productivity measure.

contextCards.context: In a 2024 survey of 2,000 respondents across the United States, Brazil, Germany, and India, more than 97% reported having used AI coding tools at work at some point.
contextCards.caveat: Survey usage at some point; it does not measure frequency, authorization, or production deployment.
